```{r, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(gganimate)
library(gifski)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(caret)
setwd("C:/Users/student/OneDrive - Bryant University/Documents/GitHub/Projects_in_R/Assignments")

df = read_csv("Data/midterm.csv")
names_na = names(df)[colSums(is.na(df)) > 0]
df = df %>% select(-all_of(names_na))

df = df %>% mutate(provider_name = case_when(
  provider == 7201 ~ "Newport",
  provider == 7202 ~ "St. Joseph Health Services of RI",
  provider == 7203 ~ "Memorial",
  provider == 7204 ~ "Miriam",
  provider == 7205 ~ "Rhode Island Hospital",
  provider == 7206 ~ "Roger Williams",
  provider == 7209 ~ "South County",
  provider == 7210 ~ "Kent County",
  provider == 7211 ~ "Westerly",
  provider == 7212 ~ "Rehab of RI",
  provider == 7213 ~ "Landmark Medical Center",
  provider == 7214 ~ "Women and Infants",
  provider == 7215 ~ "Bradley",
  provider == 7216 ~ "Butler"
))

df = df %>% mutate(season = case_when(
  moa %in% c(3, 4, 5)   ~ "Spring",
  moa %in% c(6, 7, 8)   ~ "Summer",
  moa %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Fall",
  moa %in% c(12, 1, 2)  ~ "Winter"
))
```

# Part 2: Visualization

## Patients Admitted by Month

Admissions are fairly even across months, with October the highest.

```{r}
df %>% ggplot() + geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = factor(moa))) + labs(title = "Patients Admitted by Month", x = "Month", y = "Number of Patients", caption = "Source: RI Hospital Discharge Data 2018")
```

## Male Patients Admitted by Month

Male admissions follow the same pattern; October is again the highest.

```{r}
df %>% filter(sex == 1) %>% ggplot() + geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = factor(moa))) + labs(title = "Male Patients Admitted by Month", x = "Month", y = "Number of Patients", caption = "Source: RI Hospital Discharge Data 2018")
```

## Teenage Male Patients by Month

Admissions of male teenagers (13–19) by month.

```{r}
df %>% filter(sex == 1, age >= 13, age <= 19) %>% ggplot() + geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = factor(moa))) + labs(title = "Teenage Male Patients by Month", x = "Month", y = "Number of Patients", caption = "Source: RI Hospital Discharge Data 2018")
```

## Female Patients in October by Provider

Rhode Island Hospital and Women and Infants see the most female patients.

```{r}
df %>% filter(sex == 2, moa == 10) %>% ggplot() + geom_bar(mapping = aes(y = provider_name)) + labs(title = "Female Patients in October by Provider", x = "Number of Patients", y = "Provider", caption = "Source: RI Hospital Discharge Data 2018")
```

## Patient Age by Sex

Comparison of the age distribution of male and female patients.

```{r}
df %>% ggplot() + geom_boxplot(mapping = aes(x = factor(sex), y = age)) + labs(title = "Patient Age by Sex", x = "Sex (1 = Male, 2 = Female)", y = "Age", caption = "Source: RI Hospital Discharge Data 2018")
```

## Average Patient Age by Month

Average age stays about the same throughout the year.

```{r}
df %>% group_by(moa) %>% summarise(avg_age = mean(age)) %>% ggplot() + geom_col(mapping = aes(x = factor(moa), y = avg_age)) + labs(title = "Average Patient Age by Month", x = "Month", y = "Average Age", caption = "Source: RI Hospital Discharge Data 2018")
```

## Total Charges by Provider

Rhode Island Hospital has by far the highest total charge, since it is one of the largest hospitals.

```{r}
df %>% group_by(provider_name) %>% summarise(total_charge = sum(tot)) %>% ggplot() + geom_col(mapping = aes(x = total_charge, y = provider_name)) + labs(title = "Total Charges by Provider", x = "Total Charge ($)", y = "Provider", caption = "Source: RI Hospital Discharge Data 2018")
```

## Average Charge for Teenage Males by Provider

Average charges vary a lot between providers.

```{r}
df %>% filter(sex == 1, age >= 13, age <= 19) %>% group_by(provider_name) %>% summarise(avg_charge = mean(tot)) %>% ggplot() + geom_col(mapping = aes(x = avg_charge, y = provider_name)) + labs(title = "Average Charge for Teenage Males by Provider", x = "Average Charge ($)", y = "Provider", caption = "Source: RI Hospital Discharge Data 2018")
```

## Average Length of Stay by Season

Average stay is about 5 days and is similar across seasons.

```{r}
df %>% group_by(season) %>% summarise(avg_los = mean(los)) %>% ggplot() + geom_col(mapping = aes(x = season, y = avg_los)) + labs(title = "Average Length of Stay by Season", x = "Season", y = "Average Length of Stay (days)", caption = "Source: RI Hospital Discharge Data 2018")
```

## Length of Stay vs. Total Charge

Longer stays generally lead to higher charges.

```{r}
df %>% ggplot() + geom_point(mapping = aes(x = los, y = tot)) + labs(title = "Length of Stay vs. Total Charge", x = "Length of Stay (days)", y = "Total Charge ($)", caption = "Source: RI Hospital Discharge Data 2018")
```

## Animation: Average Charge by Provider and Season

How the average charge at each provider changes across the seasons.

```{r}
g = df %>% group_by(season, provider_name) %>% summarise(avg_charge = mean(tot)) %>% ggplot() + geom_col(mapping = aes(x = avg_charge, y = provider_name)) + transition_states(season) + labs(title = "Average Charge by Provider - Season: {closest_state}", x = "Average Charge ($)", y = "Provider", caption = "Source: RI Hospital Discharge Data 2018")

animate(g)
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
df2 = read_csv("Data/midterm.csv") %>% select(tot, age, sex, raceethn, provider, moa, mod, admtype, campus, los)
df2 = df2 %>% filter(!is.na(raceethn), !is.na(admtype)) %>% drop_na()
df2 = df2 %>% mutate(target = ifelse(tot < median(tot), "low", "high")) %>% select(-tot)
df2 = df2 %>% mutate(target = factor(target),
                     sex = factor(sex), raceethn = factor(raceethn),
                     provider = factor(provider), moa = factor(moa),
                     mod = factor(mod), admtype = factor(admtype),
                     campus = factor(campus))
set.seed(2018)
splitIndex = createDataPartition(df2$target, p = 0.1, list = FALSE)
df_train = df2[splitIndex, ]
df_test = df2[-splitIndex, ]

trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5)
tree = train(target ~ ., data = df_train, method = "rpart", trControl = trControl, tuneLength = 5)
forest = train(target ~ ., data = df_train, method = "ranger", trControl = trControl, tuneLength = 3)
```

# Part 3: Predictive Models

## Q4: Model Comparison

Target: total charge **high** vs. **low** (split at the median). Decision tree vs. random forest, 5-fold cross-validation.

```{r}
results = resamples(list(Tree = tree, Forest = forest))
bwplot(results)
```

The random forest has higher accuracy than the decision tree.

## Q5: Final Model on Test Data

The final model is the **random forest**. Its accuracy on the 90% test set:

```{r}
pred = predict(forest, df_test)
confusionMatrix(pred, df_test$target, positive = "high")
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
df3 = read_csv("Data/midterm.csv") %>% select(los, age, sex, raceethn, provider, moa, admtype, campus) %>% drop_na()
df3 = df3 %>% mutate(target = ifelse(los > median(los), "long", "short")) %>% select(-los)
df3 = df3 %>% mutate(target = factor(target),
                     sex = factor(sex), raceethn = factor(raceethn),
                     provider = factor(provider), moa = factor(moa),
                     admtype = factor(admtype), campus = factor(campus))
set.seed(2018)
splitIndex = createDataPartition(df3$target, p = 0.1, list = FALSE)
df_train = df3[splitIndex, ]
df_test = df3[-splitIndex, ]
tree_model = rpart(target ~ ., data = df_train)
tree = train(target ~ ., data = df_train, method = "rpart", trControl = trControl, tuneLength = 5)
forest = train(target ~ ., data = df_train, method = "ranger", trControl = trControl, tuneLength = 3)
```

## Q6: New Target - Length of Stay

New target: length of stay **long** vs. **short** (split at the median). The decision tree:

```{r}
rpart.plot(tree_model)
```

## Q6: Variable Importance

When length of stay is the target, provider is the most important variable.

```{r}
barplot(tree_model$variable.importance, las = 2, main = "Variable Importance (Decision Tree)")
```

## Q6: Model Comparison

```{r}
results = resamples(list(Tree = tree, Forest = forest))
bwplot(results)
```

The random forest again does better than the tree.

## Q6: Final Model on Test Data

```{r}
pred = predict(forest, df_test)
confusionMatrix(pred, df_test$target, positive = "long")
```

# Challenges

## Challenges and Fixes

- **Large SAS file was slow to load** → filtered to 2018, kept needed columns, and saved a smaller CSV.
- **Missing values** → dropped columns with NAs; used `drop_na()` for the modeling data.
- **Provider codes were just numbers** → mapped them to hospital names with `case_when()`.
- **Random forest took a long time to train** → trained on the 10% training set with `tuneLength = 3`.
- **Messages and warnings cluttered the output** → turned them off with `message=FALSE, warning=FALSE`.
